title: Getting started
markdown:
## **Register an account**

Everyone who uses the platform should register their own account. Recommended registration practices:
- **Username:** Use an English name, the pinyin of your name, an employee ID, or a phone number. Usernames must be globally unique.
- **Nickname:** Use the name your colleagues normally call you, such as your real name, a familiar nickname, or an English name. This makes it easier to identify the right person when managing permissions or collaborating.
- **Email:** Use your internal company email address.

## **Create or join a Workspace**

### **Onboard a new project**

To onboard a project, create a new Workspace. Each project is isolated in its own Workspace. Here, a project means an independent system, such as a corporate website, supply chain management system, or visitor management system. One project can contain any number of frontend and backend Git repositories.

### **Join an existing project**

If someone on your team has already created the Workspace, you can join it in either of two ways:
1. Switch to “All Workspaces” on the Workspace list page, find the Workspace, and select “Request access”. A Workspace administrator approves the request in “Member management”.
2. Ask a Workspace administrator (the creator or a member with administrator access) to search for your nickname or login name in “Member management” and add you.

## **Use the platform**

### **Connect an Agent to the platform**

Open “Profile settings” at the top right, select “MCP tokens”, and create an MCP token. Configure this MCP connection in Qoder/Qoder CN. You can then use Qoder/Qoder CN to operate the platform: create Work items, analyze Delivery errors, or configure Squads, Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, and Executors. AutoWonder is AI Native; we recommend using an Agent for complex and repetitive operations.

![MCP client configuration](/help/assets/02-en-US.png "")

After configuring MCP, ask your Agent to “Use AutoWonder MCP to operate the ‘XXX’ Workspace”. We recommend installing the `auto-wonder.zip` Skill in your Agent tool. For later operations on AutoWonder, enter `/auto-wonder` in the Agent.

[auto-wonder.zip](/help/assets/auto-wonder.zip)

The Skill content is shown below. It instructs your Agent to use the AutoWonder platform MCP to perform operations.
```markdown
---
name: auto-wonder
description: Use when the user invokes auto-wonder or asks to perform an operation through the AutoWonder platform.
---

# AutoWonder

Use the AutoWonder platform MCP to perform operations.

```

Example: ask `/auto-wonder` to analyze whether the Agents, their SDLC definitions, repository configuration, repository relationships, and Agent repository bindings in the Standard Automated Delivery Squad of the “XXX” Workspace are complete. Ask whether the Squad can deliver Work items automatically, which stages hand off automatically, and which need human intervention.
```markdown
/auto-wonder Analyze whether the Agents, their SDLC definitions, repository configuration, repository relationships, and Agent repository bindings in the Standard Automated Delivery Squad of the "XXX" Workspace are complete. Can the entire Squad deliver Work items automatically? Which stages hand off automatically, and which require human intervention?
```

**Project administrators:** If you administer a project Workspace and are responsible for onboarding the project, configure its Squads, Agents, SDLC workflows, repositories, and repository relationships for the actual project. This defines the AI automated Delivery pipeline and is a critical step best performed by someone who knows the project well. Continue to optimize, iterate on, and maintain the configuration to improve Delivery efficiency and quality and reduce token consumption. See the “Project onboarding” chapter for configuration instructions.

**Project team members:** If you work on development or testing and are responsible for Delivery, focus on the “Work items”, “Scheduled tasks”, and “Execution records” modules in the Delivery section to submit, clarify, and deliver requirements.

## Step 2: Follow the Workspace setup guide

In your new Workspace, follow the setup guide to initialize the Workspace and onboard your project.

## Tips

- **Avoid skipping the setup guide** unless you know the platform well and can onboard a project from scratch. If you skip it, you’ll need to create another Workspace to see the guide again.
- **Avoid selecting “Don’t remind me again” before skipping the guide** unless you can onboard projects on your own. If you do, the guide will no longer appear in new Workspaces you create with this account.

title: IM integration
markdown:
## **Configure the platform bot**

A platform administrator first configures the platform channel and bots. Each workspace administrator then binds their group chat. The following steps use DingTalk as an example.

1. Open “Platform configuration” from the Workspace list, then select “Message channels”. Choose the IM type first and confirm any channel switch as prompted. System notifications and group-chat access across all workspaces follow the current platform channel.
2. Follow the page instructions to configure the notification bot and group-chat bot separately. The notification bot sends personal system notifications; the group-chat bot supports workspace collaboration. They must use different application identities.
3. For the DingTalk group-chat bot, enter its AppKey, AppSecret, and RobotCode, enable the shared group-chat bot, and save it. Complete and save the notification form separately. Credentials are managed at platform level; workspace administrators do not enter them again.





## **Set your Employee ID**

Every platform user should set their Employee ID in “Personal settings” so system notifications can reach them through the configured IM tool.



## **Bind a workspace group chat**

After the platform bot is configured, a workspace administrator opens “Integrations → Messaging channels” in the current workspace. New group-chat bindings use the platform shared bot rather than separate application credentials for each workspace.

1. Add the platform group-chat bot to the target DingTalk group. Type @ and select the bot, then send the group-information command shown on the integration page. Copy the complete group ID from its reply.
2. Create a new binding and enter the group ID. DingTalk requires the message conversationId (usually starting with cid), not the numeric group number shown in the client. Keep the entire value.
3. Select a **Project Manager Agent without an SDLC workflow** as the linked digital worker, then save the DingTalk binding. The Project Manager is the single point of communication with users: it reviews, coordinates, and analyzes workspace requirements and Work items, and delegates to other Agents when needed. Do not use an Agent assigned to a specific SDLC delivery step as the group-chat entry point.
4. @mention the bot in the target group and confirm that the linked Project Manager responds. If it does not, check the current platform channel, whether the shared group-chat bot is enabled and connected, and the group ID and Agent binding. Platform access status alone does not verify every group or guarantee that every message is processed or delivered.

![Workspace message channel integration and new binding action](/help/assets/14-en-US.png "")

title: Best practices
markdown:
## **Manage account permissions**
1. **Change the default `admin` account password promptly after the first login.**
2. After deployment, you can use the initialized `admin` account to configure the platform. For daily use, sign in with your own registered account so audit logs identify the operator. If you need to manage the platform, grant your personal account the platform administrator role instead of continuing to use the shared `admin` account.
3. Platform administrators can grant that role to others as needed in “Platform configuration”. We recommend giving platform administrator access to the person responsible for the platform.
4. Give project administrator access only to people who maintain the project configuration. Allowing everyone to modify configuration and register Executors can create confusion.

## **Executors**
1. For initial setup, register Executors on one computer, with one Executor per Agent. Avoid registering too many: Delivery tasks are automatically scheduled across available Executors according to load. During debugging and validation, tasks may otherwise be sent to another machine and stop if it shuts down or sleeps, making debugging harder.
2. After validation, run production Executors in an environment that can operate continuously, such as a Linux server or Mac mini. Windows is not recommended for long-term operation because problems such as garbled text can occur. If Windows is required, install WSL and register Executors in its Linux environment.
3. Install every project dependency in the Executor environment. For a Java project, for example, install JDK, Maven, and Git. Development, testing, and validation all run in that environment.

## **Qoder accounts**
1. A personal account is suitable for signing in to Qoder CLI during initial testing and validation. For stable long-term operation, apply for an account representing the team and allocate sufficient Credits for production Delivery. Delivery consumes the Credits of the Qoder account signed in on the Executor, rather than those of the person who submits the Work item.

## **Work item Delivery**
1. Submit requirements and bug fixes as Work items. Delivery runs around each Work item, the configured Agents, and their SDLC workflows.
2. For questions during Delivery, such as progress, error causes, or solutions, @mention the relevant Agent in the Work item's comments.

## **Optimize costs**
1. For non-urgent production requirements, schedule Delivery during off-peak hours, such as 10 p.m., to benefit from applicable off-peak discounts and reduce Credit consumption.
2. Project administrators should continuously use the platform's workflow optimization capabilities to improve the automated Delivery pipeline. This can improve Delivery efficiency and greatly reduce Credit consumption.
3. Practical experience shows that Flash models can deliver high quality for deterministic execution tasks. Use flagship models for Agents whose work determines Delivery quality, such as Clarification and code review. Flash models are recommended for other Agents, including full-stack development, deployment operations, and test case execution, to improve efficiency and reduce Credit consumption.

title: Frequently asked questions
markdown:
Q: I cannot see the detailed Delivery process in AutoWonder and feel uncertain. What should I focus on?

A: AutoWonder's AI Native SDLC changes software Delivery fundamentally compared with Vibe Coding. Agents handle the entire requirement Delivery process using the preconfigured workflow. People focus on Clarification and acceptance of the final results rather than every intermediate detail. This frees people to work on higher-value system architecture, business architecture, and business functionality, and allows one person to drive Delivery of multiple requirements in parallel.

Q: Our team wants to keep separate product, development, and testing roles. How should we configure Delivery?

A: Teams moving to full-stack development can use one Squad to deliver the whole requirement. Teams retaining traditional role-based work can design separate Squads, Agents, and SDLC workflows for their needs. Each role uses its own Squad to complete its part around the same Work item, then reaches a human decision stage. You can also specify the downstream people in the SDLC workflow; they receive an IM notification and continue Delivery using their own Squad. Once the platform's IM tool is configured, hand off to the relevant user's registered username in the SDLC workflow to send collaboration notifications. You can also manually @mention a person in Work item comments and ask them to take over the next stages.

Q: What should I do if a Work item encounters an error during Delivery?

A: @mention the relevant Agent and ask what went wrong and how to resolve it. A desktop Agent connected to AutoWonder MCP can also analyze the Work item's error. If you suspect a platform issue, connect the Agent to the AutoWonder source to investigate. If it confirms a platform defect, report the analysis to Alibaba Cloud for a fix.

Q: How many Work items can one Executor run at once, and when should I add capacity?

A: By default, each Executor for each Agent can run up to ten tasks concurrently; additional tasks queue. Because each Work item's workflow runs serially, a Squad's registered Executors can be understood as handling ten Work items at a time. If your computer or server has enough capacity, you can register multiple sets of Executors on one machine. Each task uses an isolated session, so tasks do not interfere even on the same machine. When load becomes too high, add another machine and register Executors there; the platform will schedule new tasks to it. Executors are stateless and can scale horizontally, for example by adding multiple Mac mini machines to the same project for Delivery.

Q: How should we configure project knowledge bases and development standards?

A: For business logic already expressed in code, we do not recommend maintaining a separate knowledge base or explanation: code is the best documentation. For development standards or internal terminology, use one of these approaches:
1. Maintain the documents in source repositories. Specify in the Agent definition which repository content to read and at which stage.
2. Package the development standards as a Skill, upload it to AutoWonder, and bind it to the relevant Agents. Explain in each Agent definition when to use the Skill, which knowledge to retrieve, or which standards to follow.
3. Expose your internal knowledge base as a Skill or MCP, upload it to AutoWonder, and bind it to the relevant Agents. Update the Agent instructions to integrate the enterprise knowledge base.

Q: What should I do if a Work item's workflow takes too long?

A: Consider these situations:
1. Execution time depends on the automated Delivery pipeline definition. A long workflow takes longer to complete.
2. Agent and SDLC definitions often have substantial room for improvement. Missing environment dependencies or imprecise workflow instructions can cause extra reasoning and retries, wasting time and Credits. Use an Agent to analyze and improve the definitions continuously. Also use the platform's workflow optimization capabilities to identify and improve pipeline configuration.
3. Replace model reasoning with scripts wherever scripts can accomplish the work.

AutoWonder's AI Native SDLC is a form of software Delivery for the AI era. People clarify requirements and make decisions; the automated pipeline handles the connecting and manual work that previously required people. You can focus on requirements and results instead of watching every execution step.

Focus on whether Delivery quality meets requirements, whether the automated production pipeline runs efficiently in the current environment, and whether Credit optimization meets your needs.

During working hours, people and Agents deliver requirements together. At night, Agents continue Delivery using Scheduled tasks and the automated pipeline, and you accept the results the next day. This enables 7×24-hour Delivery, with one person driving continuous Delivery of multiple requirements in parallel.

Q: What should I do if Delivery quality does not meet requirements?

A: Improve the automated pipeline for the specific problems. Use unit, integration, E2E, feature, and Playwright tests to protect quality. Add development standards and requirements to the pipeline through Skills, project documents, and similar mechanisms.

Q: What should I do if the frontend does not match the intended design closely enough?

A: Try these approaches:
1. Define frontend development standards, including element colors, spacing, and pagination styles, to improve quality.
2. Confirm the frontend design as HTML, then upload the HTML to the Work item so subsequent development can build directly from it. Design and confirmation of the HTML can be stages in the automated Delivery pipeline; arrange the workflow as needed.
